newsitem.title: ANTIGUA AND BARBUDA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA UNDER PRESSURE DESPITE JAYASURIYA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA UNDER PRESSURE DESPITE JAYASURIYA.

text.p: Sri Lanka continued to experience problems against the West Indian pace attack on the opening day of the first test on Friday, despite an excellent 85 off 115 balls from opener Sanath Jayasuriya.

At tea the Sri Lankans were 180 for five but had also lost middle-order batsman Hashan Tillekeratne, forced to retire hurt on one when he was struck on the right forearm by a rising delivery by West Indies' skipper Courtney Walsh.
Resuming after lunch on 72 for three, Sri Lanka lost the wickets of captain Arjuna Ranatunga, who was run out for 42 and opener Jayasuriya, bowled by off-spinner Carl Hooper for 85.

Jayasuriya, who batted for 233 minutes, striking nine fours and two sixes, added 109 for the fourth-wicket with Ranatunga before the Sri Lankan captain attempted a single off a Walsh no-ball and was beaten by a Curtly Ambrose throw from mid-off to wicket-keeper Courtney Browne.
Ambrose had been the destroyer before lunch with three wickets for 31 runs off 12 overs, and now needs just two more to reach 300 in test cricket.
Score: Sri Lanka 180-5 (S.Jayasuriya 85) v West Indies.
